title: How to organize the stair and floor path | Stair Landing
description:
The treads, runner, handrail and lighting that carry every person in the house between floors, several times a day, often with their arms full.

This is the Stair and Floor Path in the Stair Landing. About 30-45 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Every tread bare from nose to riser, including the bottom three steps that usually stage things. The runner lies flat with no lifted corner at the turn. The handrail runs unbroken and unobstructed from the top newel post to the bottom, with no bag, coat or dog lead hung on either post. Both switches work, so the top step and the bottom step are lit before you take them.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Nothing lives on stairs.
Straighten: The one thing that must stay reachable here is the handrail, so strip both newel posts of coats, bags and lead
Shine: Vacuum the tread noses, the crevice where each tread meets its riser, and along the stringer where a runner is
Safety: Walk the flight slowly and test as you go: press each tread nose for movement, tug each runner edge, and grip
Standardize: The standard is one sentence anyone in the house can check: bare treads, full width, lit at both ends, rail cl
Sustain: The last person up at night takes the flight with one hand on the rail and carries whatever is sitting on a tr

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Bare treads at full width, runner flat and fixed the whole way, handrail clear from newel to newel, and working light at both ends.
